A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Vision Transformer continual-learning work, renamed from ArtiHippo to CHEEM. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures, and tables, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original VDD and 5-Dataset experiments, baseline comparisons, architecture analyses, and component and sampling ablations.

after.justification: V4 reports original benchmark results and ablations, including quantitative task-order comparisons and expanded shortcut-adapter experiments.

M1.justification: The projection-layer memory, four operations, hybrid adapter, and NAS pipeline remain. V4 removes v3 Section 3.3's task-prompt integration variant. The reported sampling procedure also changes locally: v3 retains an unchanged mean token when reusing an expert, whereas v4 Sections 2.2–2.2.2 retain task-specific means for shared experts and sample previous tasks.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten VDD tasks and five tasks in the 5-Dataset benchmark. Task-to-task transfer on VDD already appears in v3 Section 4.4. Additional task orders and adapter controls change evaluation design, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The principal baseline families remain unchanged, including L2P, S-Prompts, L2G, SupSup, EFT, LL, EWC, L2 regularization, and replay. However, L2P reference rows are removed from the prompt-count ablation comparisons: v3 Tables 8–9 versus v4 Tables 14–15. L2P remains in the main benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: The default VDD supernet budget changes from 150 epochs in v3 Appendix J.1 to 100 in v4 Appendix C. Adapter controls expand from ImageNet-to-Omniglot to full VDD sequences under both sequential and task-to-task protocols, and quantitative evaluation covers four alternate task orders. These substantially revise the experimental design within retained datasets.

E4.justification: V4 Appendix E adds quantitative HEE-versus-PE comparisons across four alternate task orders and expands shortcut-adapter accuracy and efficiency analyses across both learning protocols. V3 offered one qualitative alternate-order example and a two-task shortcut test. Conversely, v3's parameter-growth analysis and cosine-normalization diagnostics are removed.

E5.justification: V4 Table 12 reports uncertainty for shortcut-comparison resource costs, including FLOP growth, whereas v3's shortcut table and FLOP discussion give point estimates. The main three-seed VDD and five-order 5-Dataset reporting conventions remain. The PDFs do not establish an increase in repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: The main VDD result changes from 82.60±0.55 at 150 epochs to 83.44±0.50 at 100 epochs, so this is not a same-setting improvement. The 5-Dataset result changes from 94.33±0.45 to 94.82±0.02. Component-ablation values change, task-order and shortcut results expand, and the 83.55±0.09 prompt-integrated result disappears. The task-to-task result of 84.65±0.33 and many baseline scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V4 revises the formal expert representation and sampling description to accommodate task-specific means for shared experts. It also removes v3 Appendix I's explicit DARTS mixture and SPOS optimization formulations. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs; the changes concern limited mathematical definitions and background formulations.

C1.justification: The central claims about projection-layer memory, hierarchical NAS, zero forgetting under task IDs, and strong benchmark performance remain. V4 drops v3's fourth contribution claiming demonstrated gains from combining the method with prompting; this combination becomes future work in Section 3.1.1.

C2.justification: V4 Section 3.3 explains why task-ID inference is difficult for overlapping VDD tasks and proposes combining token information across layers. It also interprets sequential-versus-transfer architecture differences as room for improving NAS. V3's sublinear parameter-growth interpretation and explicit fairness qualification for regularization/replay comparisons are removed.

D1.justification: V4 discloses the 20-epoch budgets for the retained regularization/replay results and a replay coreset of 30 samples per class. Most architecture, preprocessing, optimizer, and search details remain. V3's explicit training-log locations, checkpoint-release statement, and prompt-integration training details are omitted; actual external resource availability cannot be established from these PDFs.

R1.justification: V4 adds references such as CODA-Prompt, DER, D3Former, and lifelong ViT, alongside new positioning against class-incremental assumptions. It removes neuroscience references and discussions of Veniat et al. and task-difficulty-aware allocation. The central relationship to L2G and SPOS remains; bibliographic metadata updates do not constitute additional research changes.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively rewritten around CHEEM and task synergies. Related work moves after experiments, limitations receive a dedicated subsection, and the appendices are substantially reorganized and condensed. This exceeds a simple method rename.

P2.justification: V4 rearranges the overview diagrams, adds a task-sequence illustration, and expands architecture displays into multiple seed and task-order panels with parameter/FLOP columns. Tables gain training-budget and dataset information, and the sampling-budget plots are redesigned. The parameter-growth plot and six-panel normalization diagnostic disappear.

improvement.justification: V4 strengthens support for the central NAS method through quantitative task-order robustness tests and full-VDD shortcut accuracy/cost comparisons, addressing gaps left by v3's qualitative order example and two-task adapter study. Its task-ID limitations are also clearer. These provide a limited net improvement despite losing normalization and growth diagnostics and some reproducibility disclosures. Higher headline accuracy alone does not establish improvement because the VDD training budget changes.
